task.title: Mask elements
task.shortdesc: A mask makes parts of an element transparent, in steps that go from fully visible to fully hidden. You draw the mask with a mask element and combine several masks in layers.

info.p: A mask element holds the shapes, text and images of the mask. You name it in the mask-image property of the element you want to mask, as url(#id). The shorthand mask takes the same reference. You can set it on shapes, text, images, groups and use elements.

The mask is drawn in the coordinates of the masked element, so it moves when the element moves. Where the mask is light the element shows, where it is dark the element is transparent, and the steps between them make the element partly transparent. A gradient in a mask gives a fade.
A reference to an element that is not a mask element, or to nothing, is a layer that is fully transparent. When it is the only layer, it hides the element.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <linearGradient id="ramp"> <stop offset="0" stop-color="#ffffff"/> <stop offset="1" stop-color="#000000"/> </linearGradient> <mask id="fade-out"> <rect x="120" y="10" width="95" height="70" fill="url(#ramp)"/> </mask> </defs> <rect class="faded" x="120" y="10" width="95" height="70" fill="#1d4f7a"/>

info.p: A mask measures either the luminance or the alpha of what it holds. By default it is the luminance, multiplied by the alpha, so a black shape hides and a white one shows, and a transparent shape hides. The mask-type property of the mask element can be luminance or alpha. With alpha, a black shape shows as much as a white one, and only the empty parts hide.

The mask-mode property of the masked element decides for itself. Its value can be luminance or alpha, which replace the mask-type of the mask element, or match-source, the initial value, which uses it.

step.cmd: Set the region and the units of a mask

info.p: A mask has a region, given by x, y, width and height, outside which the element is hidden. By default the region is the box of the masked element made 10% larger on every side, as the initial values -10% and 120% say. The numbers of the region are fractions of the box, until you write maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse", which makes them user units. A region without width or height hides the element.
The numbers inside the mask are user units. With maskContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" they are fractions of the box of the element, so the same mask fits elements of every size.

Masks can hold other masks and clips: an element inside a mask can have its own mask and clip-path. An element can have a clip and a mask at once, and then also an opacity. The clip is applied first, then the mask, then the opacity.

You can list several masks in mask-image, separated by commas. Each is a layer, and the first one is the top one. The property mask-composite says how each layer combines with the layers below it. It takes a list too, with one value for each layer except the lowest one, which has nothing under it:

ul.li: add, the initial value, shows what either layer shows.
subtract shows what the layer shows and the layers below do not.
intersect shows what the layer and the layers below both show.
exclude shows what only one of them shows.

info.p: A value of none in the list is a layer that is fully transparent. It still counts as a layer, so mask-image: url(#a), none with mask-composite: intersect hides the element. When mask-mode or mask-composite has fewer values than there are layers, the list repeats until there are enough. When it has more, the last ones are not used.

fig.title: Two masks, and what each operator shows

image.alt: Two bars overlap, one yellow and one blue, which are the two masks. Four dark blue rectangles show what remains with add, subtract, intersect and exclude.

info.p: The shorthand mask sets all the layers at once.

step.cmd: Mask with an image or a gradient

info.p: A layer of mask-image does not have to be a mask element. It can be the URL of an image file, a gradient, image-set(), image() or cross-fade(). An image layer uses the alpha of the image by default: where the image is opaque the element shows, and where it is transparent the element is hidden. With mask-mode: luminance the layer uses the luminance of the image instead.

An image layer is placed in a box of the element, like a background. The box is the stroke box by default, the area that the element and its outline cover. Five properties control the layer, and each takes a list with one value for each layer:

ul.li: mask-origin chooses the box that the position and the size refer to. It can be fill-box or content-box or padding-box, which are all the fill box, stroke-box or border-box or margin-box, which are all the stroke box, or view-box, the viewport of the drawing.
mask-clip chooses the box in which the layer paints. It takes the same values, and no-clip, which does not limit it.
mask-size sets the size of the image: auto, cover, contain, or one or two lengths or percentages.
mask-position places the image in the origin box. right bottom puts it in the bottom right corner and center centers it.

mask-repeat repeats the image. With repeat it covers the area, with space it puts as many whole images as fit with equal gaps, with round it stretches the images to fit a whole number of times, and with no-repeat it is drawn once.

info.p: A gradient has no size of its own, so with mask-size: auto it fills the origin box. The mask hides everything that the layers do not cover.
